questions.title: What exactly is the non‑uniformity in RoPE dimensions referred to in LongRoPE?
questions.question_body:
The paper repeatedly mentions that RoPE dimensions exhibit "substantial non‑uniformities" and that lower dimensions (high frequency) and higher dimensions (low frequency) should be treated differently during interpolation. I am not clear on what metric or property defines this non‑uniformity. Is it related to the frequency 
\(\theta_i = \theta^{-2i/d}\) itself, the information entropy of each dimension, or something else? How can we quantify or visualize this non‑uniformity to understand why a uniform scaling factor \(\lambda\) is sub‑optimal?

questions.title: How does the function \(\mathbb{I}(\hat{\lambda}_i, \hat{n})\) work for the initial token positions?
questions.question_body: Equation (4) defines \(\mathbb{I}(\hat{\lambda}_i, \hat{n})\) as 1 for positions \(n < \hat{n}\) and \(1/\lambda_i\) otherwise. I am confused about the intuition: why keep the first \(\hat{n}\) tokens unchanged? How does this relate to the claim that "initial tokens receive large attention scores"? Also, is \(\hat{n}\) a shared threshold across all RoPE dimensions or does it vary per dimension?

questions.title: Why does the monotonicity constraint \(\lambda_i \le \lambda_{i+1}\) make sense for RoPE interpolation?
questions.question_body: The search algorithm enforces that rescale factors increase monotonically with RoPE dimension index. The paper cites NTK theory as justification but does not elaborate. Could someone explain why higher‑index (lower‑frequency) dimensions should receive larger scaling factors, and what would happen if this constraint were relaxed?

questions.title: What is the exact relationship between extension ratio \(s\) and the allowed search range for each \(\lambda_i\)?
questions.question_body: In the search space description, each \(\lambda_i\) can vary from 1.0 to \(s \times 1.25\) with step 0.01. Why is the upper bound set to \(1.25 s\)? Does this correspond to a specific theoretical limit, or is it an empirical choice? How sensitive are results to this upper bound?

questions.title: How is the progressive extension from 256k to 2048k performed without additional fine‑tuning?
questions.question_body: The paper describes a three‑step pipeline: search → fine‑tune to 256k → second search to reach 2048k. I am unclear on what exactly changes between the first and second search. Are we searching a new set of \(\lambda_i\) values for the already fine‑tuned model, or are we also adjusting \(\hat{n}\)? How does this second interpolation achieve an 8× jump without any extra gradient updates?

questions.title: What is meant by "readjust LongRoPE on 8k length to recover short context performance"?
questions.question_body: After extending to 2048k, the authors perform another evolution search for short windows (4k/8k). Is this a separate set of rescale factors applied only when the input length is <=8k, or are they blended with the long‑window factors? How is this switching implemented during inference?

questions.title: Can you clarify how perplexity is used as the fitness function in the evolutionary search?
questions.question_body: The algorithm computes perplexity on a few samples from PG19 or Pile-Books3 for each candidate set of \(\lambda_i\). Are these perplexities averaged over all sampled sequences? Also, since perplexity depends on both model parameters and position embeddings, how robust is this metric given only 5–3 validation samples?

questions.title: Why does YaRN underperform PI and NTK on PG19 according to Table 1?
questions.question_body: The authors note that YaRN's perplexity spikes after 7k in an 8k context size and that it "doesn't reach the target context window length for non‑fine‑tuned LLM". Is this because YaRN's grouping of dimensions was tuned for smaller extensions, or does its extrapolation strategy inherently fail for very long sequences? How could one adapt YaRN to avoid this issue?

questions.title: "Passkey retrieval" results: why does Mistral drop from 100% to 60% at ~2048k while LLaMA2 remains >90%?
questions.question_body: In Figure 5, LongRoPE-Mistral-2048k maintains perfect accuracy up to ~1800k tokens but then falls sharply at 2048k, whereas LongRoPE-LLaMA2-2048k stays above 90% throughout. The paper attributes this partly to training length differences, but I would like a deeper explanation: is it due to model architecture, tokenizer differences, or perhaps the way RoPE frequencies interact with extremely long lengths?

questions.title: How does LongRoPE preserve performance on standard benchmarks designed for a 4k window?
questions.question_body: Table 7 shows comparable zero‑shot/few‑shot scores on ARC‑Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, etc., even after extending the context window to 2048k. What mechanisms prevent degradation in short‑context tasks? Is it solely the "short context recovery" search step, or are there other regularization effects from fine‑tuning at 256k?
